1#main: When mourning begins, and for whom they move from grave to grave. In it are 11 seifim. From when does mourning begin? From when he is buried and sealing the grave with earth is finished — mourning begins immediately and he wraps his head; but he does not remove his shoes until he reaches his house (Ramban); and now the custom is to remove shoes immediately after sealing the golel, as in siman 376: {Rama: (and see above siman 372); if he thought the grave was sealed and began mourning and afterward learned he erred — he returns and begins mourning anew (Rosh klal 27).}
2#main: One whose custom is to send the dead to another country to bury him and they do not know when he will be buried — from when they turn back from escorting, they begin counting seven and thirty and begin mourning (Rambam ch. 1 of Mourning halacha 6); and those who go with him count from when he is buried; and if the family head went with him, even those here do not count until he is buried; and the family head — meaning the household head whom all rely on and all are drawn after him — whether brother, whether minor son; and some say provided he is thirteen.
3#main: If they move the dead from grave to grave — if they buried him in the first grave on condition to remain buried there forever, but afterward decided to move him — they do not count for him except from when he was buried in the first grave, even if they cleared him within seven; but if initially they buried him on condition to move when opportunity arises — mourning begins immediately; and if they cleared him within seven, they return and count from when he is buried a second time; and if they did not clear him until after seven, his mourning already passed and they do not mourn for him again; and if initially they intended to move him from there within seven — they do not begin counting until he is buried in the second grave.
4#main: If they placed the dead in a coffin and placed it in another house because the city was under siege — they count for him seven and thirty immediately, even though they intend to bury him in the cemetery after the siege; and sealing the coffin is like burial and mourning begins immediately.
5#main: Those executed by the government whom they do not allow to be buried — from when do they begin mourning and counting seven and thirty? From when they despaired of asking the king to bury them, even though they did not despair of its being stolen.
6#main: One informed that gentiles crucified his relative in another city and he practiced mourning immediately, and afterward learned he still stands crucified — that mourning did not count for him and he returns to count from burial or from when they despaired (view of R' Yitzchak and Ramban).
7#main: One who drowned in waters that have an end, or a report went out that bandits killed him or a beast dragged him — from when do they count? From when they despaired of seeking; if they found him limb by limb and recognize him by bodily signs — they do not count until they find his head and majority, or they despaired of seeking {Rama: (baraita brought by Ramban)}; and if found after they despaired of him — relatives need not return to mourn, but sons — if they were there when he was found, they mourn that day, for it is no worse than gathering their father's bones; but if not there and heard after the day passed, they need not mourn: {Rama: If they sent their dead to another city whose law is to begin mourning when they turn back and they began mourning, and afterward the dead was seized and not buried a long time — they need not interrupt their mourning nor return to mourn afterward, for once their law is to begin immediately they need not interrupt (Mordechai end of Moed Katan).}
8#main: One whose relative died and he did not know until he came to the place where the dead was or to the burial place — if it was a near place that is a walk of ten parasangs so he could arrive in one day, even if he came on the seventh day {Rama: (and some say even if one came and the head of the house is not home, only that he went for the dead's needs — if he returns within three days it is as if he is home; and one who comes within three counts with them (and so in Tur); and one should be lenient according to this view; and whoever must count with them — even if he later returned home, he counts with them (Rashba siman 377))}; if he found comforters at the head of the household, even if they already rose to stand — since he found comforters {Rama: (meaning they still practice some mourning) (Tur and Rashba in responsum)} — it counts for him and he counts with them the completion of thirty days; and if he did not find comforters, he counts for himself; and likewise if it was a distant place, even if he came on the second day he counts for himself seven and thirty from the day he came.
9#main: In what case? When he did not hear of the death until he came; but if he learned on the second day and began mourning, he does not shorten his mourning because he came to them.
10#main: One who is a mourner and within the seven another relative died — he counts seven for the last dead and the seven days of the first mourning count toward completion of the seven.
11#main: One who prayed the evening prayer and it is still day and heard his relative died — some say he counts eight from the next day; and that day does not count.
